title: Least privilege
description:
Amaka slides a ticket across the desk: Tunde spotted `/home/intern/config/secrets.env` with world-writable perms on the training host. That is exactly the kind of misconfiguration The Griot loves. Confirm the current mode, tighten it back to least privilege (owner read/write only — nothing for group, nothing for world), then read the confirmation line Amaka stamped inside. That line is your flag.

Sankofa's policy (see `/home/intern/config/README`): every `*.env` file must be owner-only. Anything looser is an audit finding.

Reference: NIST SP 800-53r5 AC-6 Least Privilege; CIS Linux Benchmark §6.1 (file permissions).

welcome: Inspect the file's current mode, then bring it back to least privilege.
hints: What does the shell show you about a file's permissions when you ask politely?
Owner read+write with nothing for group or world is the target. Anything looser on a *.env file is a finding.

files./home/intern/README.md:
Amaka: routine hardening drill. Every sensitive file on this host must be 600 (owner rw, nothing else).
If you ever see 666 on something with the word `secret` in it, fix it before you touch anything else.
files./home/intern/config/README:
Config directory. Contains environment files consumed by the Sankofa training services.
Policy: *.env files must be mode 600. Anything looser is an audit finding.
